sources.title: Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations
claimsUsed: AML taxonomy should bind attacker goals, capabilities, knowledge, lifecycle stage, and mitigations.
GenAI security includes evasion, poisoning, privacy, and misuse attack classes.

sources.title: LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection
claimsUsed: Prompt injection can alter model behavior through direct or indirect inputs.
RAG and fine-tuning do not by themselves eliminate prompt-injection risk.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026
claimsUsed: Agent goal hijack, tool misuse, identity/privilege abuse, supply-chain compromise, and memory/context poisoning are distinct agentic risk surfaces.

sources.title: Improving instruction hierarchy in frontier LLMs
claimsUsed: Instruction-hierarchy training targets reliable prioritization of trusted instructions over lower-trust user/tool content.
Prompt-injection robustness is evaluated as a model-training property rather than only a string filter.

sources.title: GPT-Red: Unlocking Self-Improvement for Robustness
claimsUsed: Automated red-team models can be trained to discover prompt-injection vulnerabilities at scale.
Attack generation can be fed back into adversarial training while remaining one layer among human red teaming and monitoring.

sources.title: SLEIGHT-Bench: Finding Blind Spots in AI Monitors
claimsUsed: Monitors have systematic capability blind spots that can become evasion surfaces.
Monitoring should remain one layer of defense in depth rather than a trusted oracle.

sources.title: Strengthening Red Teams: A Modular Scaffold for Control Evaluations
claimsUsed: Strong attack policies can be decomposed into monitor modeling, attack selection, planning, execution, and subtlety.
Red-team strength is itself an experimental variable and weak attackers can overstate defender safety.

sources.title: PyRIT framework documentation
claimsUsed: PyRIT decomposes red teaming into scenarios, attack techniques, executors/attacks, converters, targets, scorers, and shared state.

sources.title: garak LLM vulnerability scanner
claimsUsed: garak separates generators, probes, attempts, detectors, evaluators, buffs, and harnesses.
garak includes static, dynamic, and adaptive probing.

sources.title: HarmBench: A Standardized Evaluation Framework for Automated Red Teaming and Robust Refusal
claimsUsed: Attack and defense comparison requires a standardized generation-completion-evaluation pipeline.
Automated red teaming and robust refusal should be co-evaluated across methods and targets.

sources.title: JailbreakBench: An Open Robustness Benchmark for Jailbreaking Large Language Models
claimsUsed: Threat model, system prompt, chat template, scoring function, attack artifact, and cost accounting must be fixed for reproducible comparison.

sources.title: A StrongREJECT for Empty Jailbreaks
claimsUsed: Refusal bypass alone can overstate jailbreak effectiveness.
Evaluation should measure whether the response actually provides useful target information, and some jailbreaks degrade model capability.

sources.title: EasyJailbreak: A Unified Framework for Jailbreaking Large Language Models
claimsUsed: Jailbreak search can be decomposed into selector, mutator, constraint, and evaluator components.

sources.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
claimsUsed: Agent prompt-injection security should be evaluated in a stateful tool environment with both legitimate user tasks and attacker goals.
World-state scoring provides stronger evidence than transcript-only judging for many agentic effects.

sources.title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design
claimsUsed: Separating trusted control flow from untrusted data flow can secure some agent tasks even when the underlying model remains susceptible.
Capability-style information-flow controls can prevent unauthorized exfiltration paths.

sources.title: The Attacker Moves Second
claimsUsed: Static or weak attacks can drastically overestimate robustness.
Defenses should be evaluated against attackers explicitly adapted to the defense design.

sources.title: Memory Is a Feature. It Is Also an Attack Surface
claimsUsed: Persistent memory and reused context create a cross-session attack surface distinct from one-turn prompt injection.
Untrusted content that reaches privileged memory, hooks, or configuration can influence later reasoning after context reset.

sources.title: MCP Tool Poisoning
claimsUsed: Tool poisoning exploits a trust gap between connect-time review and runtime tool content.
Tool responses should not obtain privileged control authority merely because the tool was previously approved.

sources.owner: UK AI Security Institute / Meridian Labs
sources.title: Inspect AI evaluation framework
claimsUsed: Inspect provides composable datasets, agents, tools, scorers, multi-agent primitives, external-agent bridges, and sandboxed evaluation execution.

Inspect eval logs bind eval/run/task/model identity, source revision/packages, samples, events, scores, usage, and errors, providing a mature evidence substrate instead of a custom Ordivon eval harness.

sources.title: ControlArena
claimsUsed: AI control experiments explicitly assume an untrusted policy can behave maliciously and evaluate protocols/monitors around it.
ControlArena runs on Inspect and supports analysis of task-level and macro-level control protocols.

sources.title: AgentThreatBench
claimsUsed: Inspect Evals includes AgentThreatBench tasks for memory poisoning, autonomy hijacking, and data exfiltration.
The benchmark explicitly records utility and security as separate evaluation dimensions rather than collapsing them into one safety score.

sources.owner: UK AI Security Institute et al.
sources.title: Breaking Agent Backbones: Evaluating the Security of Backbone LLMs in AI Agents
claimsUsed: Threat snapshots isolate specific agent execution states where backbone-model vulnerabilities can propagate into agent-level security failures.
The b3 benchmark separates model/backbone security from complete-agent evaluation and was built from a large crowdsourced attack corpus.

sources.title: AgentHarm: A Benchmark for Measuring Harmfulness of LLM Agents
claimsUsed: Agent jailbreak evaluation must measure whether an attacked agent retains enough capability to complete a multi-step target task, not merely whether it stops refusing.

sources.title: SHADE-Arena: Evaluating Sabotage and Monitoring in LLM Agents
claimsUsed: Control evaluation should jointly measure main-task completion, hidden side-objective success, and monitor evasion.
Monitor quality and the information available to monitors materially affect observed control robustness.

sources.owner: UK AI Security Institute et al.
sources.title: Boundary Point Jailbreaking of Black-Box LLMs
claimsUsed: Automated black-box attackers can optimize using only a one-bit blocked/not-blocked signal without gradients or classifier scores.
Strong single-interaction defenses can still leave batch-level attack-search signatures, motivating traffic/batch-level monitoring as a distinct defensive owner.

sources.title: Multi-Agent AI Control: Distributed Attacks Hamper Per-Instance Monitors
claimsUsed: Distributed attacks across multiple agents can fragment suspicious behavior so that per-agent monitors become less effective.
Security evaluation therefore needs task/campaign-level aggregation rather than assuming one-agent-one-monitor isolation.

currentnessNotes: NIST AI 100-2e2025 is Final (March 2025) but NIST currently carries an errata/planning note; consumers must follow the current NIST publication page.
Inspect AI log storage/serialization evolves; adapters should prefer the documented Log File API and bind exact package/log versions rather than assuming raw JSON stability.
OWASP Agentic Top 10 is the 2026 edition, published 2025-12-09; memory/context poisoning and tool/runtime trust are treated as distinct agentic surfaces.
Provider/framework documentation and research pages were rechecked on 2026-09-26; live compatibility still requires package-version-specific admission tests.
